about: Split an amount into n parts that sum back to exactly the original. Split tender, proportional discounts and tax distribution all depend on it.

cases.name: ten dollars three ways keeps the cent
cases.about: 334 + 333 + 333 = 1000. Three times 333 loses a cent, and a cent lost per split adds up to a drawer that is short for no traceable reason.

cases.name: an exact split has no remainder to place
one part is the whole amount
the remainder goes to the earliest parts
cases.about: Pinned because it is arbitrary but must be identical in both engines: two registers splitting the same tender have to agree on which part carries the odd cent.

cases.name: a negative amount spreads the remainder the same way
cases.about: A refund split across tenders is negative, and it must sum back exactly like a sale does.

cases.name: a negative number of parts is refused
